Mount Vesuvius again is in eruption. The pheno phenomenon began with two mild shocks of earthquake, which were followed by the collapse of the eruptive cone, 200 feet high, which stood in side the crater. Lava is pouring forth profusely, and the molten mass, which covers an area of 100,000 square feet, reaches a temperature of 2,000 degrees Fahrenheit. Professor Malladra, director of the observatory on Vesuvius, descended into the crater at the beginning of the eruption, and the heat scorched his face. The photo shows, a volcanic filâme and smoke pouring out of the eruptive cone before the first real explosion. 3/7/22
A FEW FAMOUS VOLCANCOES.

It is from this volcano, on the Island of Sicily, that we get the name by which this type of mountain is known. Etna was the first volcano, for it was here that the god of thunder and lightning, Vulcan, was supposed to make his home, according to the mythology of the ancient Roman people. His forge was deep in the mountain and his bellows was supposed to fan the fires that forced smoke and flame through the vent at the top. The eruptions were the results of the anger of this god.
Mount ETNA. Sicily.

2020a - VESUVIUS. ITALY.

There is probably no volcanic peak so well known as Vesuvius. Only a few miles from the metropolis of south Italy, Naples, its fame has been sung in song and story almost since the beginings of history. On its sides燃led many thriving villages, chief among them, Pompii and Herculeneum. Shortly after the beginning of the Christian era, occurred the eruption which buried these cities deep under tons of ash and lava. There have been several eruption since and the volcano is always more or less active, its graceful plume of smoke being visabl for many miles around.
